title: vz-sched: wakeup/start vrt check uses omega*lambda instead of omega/lambda
description:
In bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js the preemption check on task start (_start_task, line 96) and wakeup (_wakeup, line 123) computes the woken/new task's effective vrt as:

    tw.vrt + schedule.class.wgup * (tw.lambda / sumlambda())

Per spec (lecture model), the comparison should add omega DIVIDED by the woken task's lambda, i.e.:

    tw.vrt + schedule.class.wgup / tw.lambda

Currently omega is multiplied by lambda (and scaled by sumlambda), giving the wrong preemption decision. Fix both call sites (lines 96 and 123) and update fixtures/snapshots under bin/lib/vz-sched/__snapshots__/ accordingly.
acceptance_criteria:
- _start_task uses wgup / lambda for the comparison
- _wakeup uses wgup / lambda for v and tw.vrtlwk strings
- Snapshots regenerated and tests pass (node bin/test.js / vz-sched suite)
close_reason: Implemented as part of netlistsvg-3l0.1: _start_task (lib.js:96) and _wakeup (lib.js:123) now use the shared wakeupV(tw) = tw.vrt + omega / tw.lambda helper. Snapshots regenerated. ADR 0001 decision #1.

title: vz-sched: add printConditions LaTeX artifact for vrt-update conditions on wakeup/start
description:
Add a new generator function printConditions(history, schedule) in bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js that emits a LaTeX itemize/aligned block listing, for every wakeup AND every task start in the run history, the conditions used to update the woken/new task's virtual runtime and the preemption comparison against the currently active task.

For each event the block should show:
  - task name (woken/started) and timestamp
  - tw.vrt before clamp
  - clamp: tw.vrt = max(tw.vrt, vmin - latency/2)
  - effective comparison value v = tw.vrt + omega / tw.lambda  (per netlistsvg-yr5.1 fix)
  - state.curr.vrt at the moment of comparison
  - decision: preempt (checkmark) or not (times)

Wire it into saveIt() in lib.js as an additional latexArtifact entry (name e.g. 'wakeup conditions', standalone/pdflatex/-r varwidth) so it is saved alongside the rt-diagram and data-table artifacts. Update fixtures/snapshots accordingly.

Implementation notes:
  - The simplest source of truth is to capture structured wakeup/start records inside _wakeup and _start_task (push to e.g. history.conditions = [{kind, time, task, vrtBefore, vrtAfter, v, currVrt, decision}, ...]) rather than re-parsing tw.vrtlwk strings.
  - Reuse the same omega/lambda formula as the (fixed) preemption check to avoid drift.
acceptance_criteria:
- New printConditions function in bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js
- Covers both _wakeup and _start_task events
- saveIt() emits the new artifact alongside existing ones
- Snapshots regenerated; vz-sched tests pass
- LaTeX renders cleanly via standalone/pdflatex
notes: Decision: implement with canonical omega/lambda formula already in place (ADR 0001). yr5.1 reduces to migrating existing _start_task/_wakeup call sites to the shared helper.
close_reason: Implemented: shared wakeupV helper (canonical omega/lambda per ADR 0001), state.conditions capture in _start_task and _wakeup, printConditions LaTeX generator wired into saveIt as 4th artifact ('wakeup conditions'). Tests pass (5/5 vz-sched, snapshots regenerated).

title: vz-sched: verify state.vmin excludes waking task's rho during wakeup
description:
In bin/lib/vz-sched/lib.js, _wakeup (line 118) reads state.vmin at line 120 to clamp the waking task's vrt:

    tw.vrt = Math.max(tw.vrt, state.vmin - schedule.class.latency / 2);

state.vmin is recomputed in _task_tick (line 154) as _.minBy(state.rbt, 'vrt').vrt. At the moment of the read on line 120 tw is still in 'blocked', so vmin does not yet include tw — but after addToRbt(tw) on line 122 the next vmin refresh will include tw.vrt, which can pull vmin down if the waking task carried a stale/low rho.

Per spec, when a task wakes up, state.vmin must not consider the rho of the waking task itself. Investigate whether:
  - vmin needs to be refreshed inside _wakeup BEFORE the clamp on line 120 (using rbt excluding tw — currently safe since tw isn't in rbt yet, but worth confirming the read isn't stale from a prior tick),
  - and/or whether subsequent vmin updates should explicitly exclude just-woken tasks for some interval.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document the expected invariant for vmin around wakeup
- If broken, fix vmin computation/refresh so the waking task's rho is excluded as required
- Snapshots regenerated and vz-sched tests pass
close_reason: Verified during 3l0.1 implementation: in _wakeup, state.vmin is read before addToRbt(tw), so tw is still in 'blocked' and structurally excluded from rbt-based vmin (mirrors Linux place_entity pre-enqueue read). Documented in code comment ('ADR 0001, decision #2') at the clamp site.
